In Google’s infrastructure model, we don't just rely on local stability; we design for its inevitable failure.

Active-Active Failover: Our Guangdong operations likely utilize an "Active-Active" architecture. If the local grid in one zone (e.g., near Guangzhou or Shenzhen) destabilizes due to fire-damaged transmission lines, traffic is shifted via Global Load Balancing (GLB) to unaffected regions (like Singapore or Taiwan) with near-zero RTO (Recovery Time Objective).

Dual-Feed & Microgrids: Most Tier 4 equivalent data centers utilize dual-utility feeds from geographically diverse substations. For a wildfire to cause a total outage, it would have to sever both paths simultaneously.

The "Diesel Gap": While we have massive on-site backup generation, the logistics concern during a wildfire is fuel replenishment. If local roads are closed due to fire, we rely on a 48–72 hour on-site reserve before "graceful degradation" of non-essential services begins.
